turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come through, have a seat. What's brought you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah, look, it's nothing much. Wife thinks my ankles are up. Bit puffy, that's all.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It is not nothing. His socks are cutting in, and he's forever in the loo.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Okay. How's it been from your side?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Couple of weeks, maybe. Ankles get a bit swollen by the arvo. I still get around fine. And yeah I wee a bit more, but I'm on that water tablet, so, you know.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any shortness of breath with it? Or pain in the chest?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Nah. No breathlessness. No chest pain. I'm not crook.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): How often are you passing urine, roughly?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, every couple of hours through the day. It's not a drama.
[SEG0010] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And he's up in the night. Twice, easy. He just shrugs it off.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Once or twice. Whatever. It's fine.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): What are you taking for the blood pressure these days?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodopine, ten milligram, every morning. And the water one, um, indapamide, two and a half, same time. I take them every day. It's for the blood pressure.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anyone in the family had blood pressure problems, diabetes, heart trouble?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Uh my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, um my brother had a heart attack round sixty, and another sister has pressure but no sugar, that's about it.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): And what's life looking like outside this? Work, food, that sort of thing.

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm a fitter down at the rail yards, twelve hour shifts, four on four off. Diet's ordinary, pies and takeaway more than I'd like to admit, not much veg. Exercise, well the job's heavy enough, I don't do any extra. Alcohol, a few beers on the days off, nothing silly.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any blood tests you remember from before?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, last year at the other place they said the cholesterol was borderline. Didn't actually tell me a number.
[SEG0020] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, the home machine doesn't match what you lot get. I've been writing them in a book.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Oh, helpful. What sort of numbers are you seeing at home?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Around one thirty over eighty. Bit less some mornings. I reckon your cuff just reads high. Not a big deal.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me take it here. Right. Today I've got 158 over 96, and your pulse is 78.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll have a look at those ankles. Mm. Both sides are puffy and it leaves a little dent. Chest sounds clear, which is good.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): What I was thinking is we nudge the indapamide up a bit, shift some of that fluid, and leave the amlodipine where it is.
[SEG0026] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He only went up to the ten milligram about a month back. Ankles came up after that. They were fine on the smaller dose.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, suppose. Still reckon it's nothing.

[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ah, that changes it for me, I won't increase the water tablet. Swelling after the higher dose is very typical of amlodipine, and those home readings sound reasonable, so more diuretic isn't the go. We'll stop the amlodipine and I'll start perindopril, four milligrams by mouth once a day, for the blood pressure. Keep the indapamide at two and a half.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Perin-whatever. If you reckon. I still think you're making a fuss.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): I hear you. All the same, I'd like a kidney blood test this week, seeing you're on a water tablet and we're starting the new one. Reception can book that today.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): More bloods. They'll just say borderline again.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll see what it shows. Book back in with me in four weeks, and bring that home book. If you get a dry cough or you feel light-headed, ring the clinic, don't sit on it.
[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll get him here. And I'll mind the book.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, yeah. We're right. Thanks.
